raw_response:
I've been farming these 16 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, and I've learned that you can't just copy what others do — you have to count your own costs and know your own soil. My land here is medium-loam with decent organic matter from years of straw return. With only me and my wife at home now, labor is tight, so I hire machinery services for tillage and harvest, but I manage the fertilizer and spraying myself.

This year I'll keep 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 6.1 mu in cotton. The wheat-maize land pays steady — I know exactly what it costs me per mu. For winter wheat, I'm using Jimai 22, an improved variety that handles our dry springs better. I'll put down 11 kg of nitrogen per mu — that's about 24 kg of urea at topdressing plus the compound fertilizer base. Phosphorus at 5 kg per mu as diammonium phosphate at sowing, and 4 kg of potassium. I irrigate four times: wintering water in late November, then jointing, heading, and grain filling — the well has good capacity, and I'd rather spend on water than lose grain weight. Three pesticide sprays: one herbicide pre-emergence, then fungicide at heading and one insecticide if aphids show up. I expect 500 kg per mu if the spring doesn't dry out too bad.

For summer maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid right after wheat harvest — no time to waste in June. It gets 14 kg nitrogen per mu, 5 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium. Three irrigations: jointing stage, large trumpet, and grain filling. Three pesticide applications. Rotary tillage after the wheat harvest, broadcast and compact. I target 600 kg per mu; last year I got 580, so I'm pushing a bit more K this year to see if that helps fill the ears better.

The 6.1 mu of cotton is my cash crop but it's labor-heavy. I use an improved Bt variety — saves me some spraying on bollworms. Cotton needs more potassium, so I give it 7 kg per mu, 11 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus. I irrigate three times: budding, flowering peak, and boll opening. Five pesticide applications total — even with Bt, you still get aphids and spider mites. I use rotary tillage before sowing in late April. I expect about 100 kg of lint per mu, maybe 350 kg seed cotton.

Everything connects to my wallet. The wheat-maize rotation is my safety net — steady food and straw, plus grain to sell. Cotton gives better cash but the inputs are higher. I'm spending about 2,800 yuan per mu on the wheat-maize system and about 3,200 per mu on cotton. If prices hold, that works. I'm not trying new varieties blindly — I saw my neighbor try a new maize hybrid last year and it lodged, so I stick with what I know.
